name: Agamaggan
summary: In the War of the Ancients, Agamaggan gave his life against the Burning Legion. His blood and fallen body gave rise to the Razorfen, now home to the quilboar.

sections.title: The War of the Ancients
sections.body: Ten thousand years ago, Agamaggan joined the fight against the Burning Legion. The mighty demigod charged with terrifying force, yet fell in the War of the Ancients. His sacrifice helped save Azeroth from ruin.

sections.title: The Razorfen and Blood Shards
sections.body:
Agamaggan fell in the southern Barrens, and his body changed the land. His blood soaked the soil, and thorny vines rose from the dry earth to form the Razorfen. The quilboar hold this ground sacred. They see Razorfen Kraul as his resting body and Razorfen Downs as his gaping skull.

Across the Barrens, crystallized Blood Shards are believed to be remnants of his spilled blood. Quilboar geomancers and shamans draw power from the lingering primal energy within them.

sections.title: Father of the Quilboar
sections.body:
The quilboar revere Agamaggan as their divine forefather. To them, the surrounding brambles are the living armor their creator left to shelter them from hostile neighbors. They believe his spirit watches over them, lending vigor to their warriors and earth magic to their geomancers.

They defend the thorns against tauren, orcs, and centaur. They believe it is their sacred duty to guard the fallen body of the boar god who birthed them.

faq.answer: Agamaggan was a colossal boar wild god and one of the Ancient Guardians from Azeroth's earliest days. He fought the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients and gave his life to help save the world.

aliases: why are there huge thorns in the barrens
faq.answer: Agamaggan's blood soaked into the earth where he fell in the southern Barrens. Thorny vines rose from the soil and formed the Razorfen, including Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs.

faq.q: What is the connection between Agamaggan and the quilboar?
faq.answer: The quilboar are Agamaggan's descendants and revere him as their creator and god. They build their settlements among the thorns and devote their shamanic rites to his memory.
Blood Shards are crystallized remnants of Agamaggan's spilled blood, found across the Barrens. Their lingering primal energy gives quilboar geomancers and shamans power.
Yes. Night elves revere Agamaggan as one of the noble Ancients who gave his life fighting the Burning Legion.

faq.q: Is Agamaggan's skull visible in the world?
faq.answer: Quilboar tradition holds that the gaping entrance to Razorfen Downs is Agamaggan's hollowed skull and jaw. They believe its maw will consume trespassers who are not loyal to their god.

angles.text: Druids honor Agamaggan as an Ancient Guardian who fought alongside Cenarius and gave his life in the War of the Ancients.
As a shaman in the Barrens, you can sense potent earth and spirit energies lingering in Agamaggan's blood and the Razorfen thorns.
As a night elf, you remember Agamaggan as the fierce demigod who gave his life against the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients.
As a member of the Horde, you face Agamaggan's quilboar children, whose devotion to their fallen god drives relentless attacks across the Barrens.
